title: Measuring Cultural Alignment Beyond the Average: A Framework for Evaluating Maternal-Health LLM Interactions in Indian Contexts

bias_targets.methodology: Administering a culturally grounded 26-item maternal health survey (MH-INDIC) to LLMs using profile-conditioned prompting, and comparing the models' cultural dimension scores (e.g., familial authority, medical trust, emotional suppression) against empirical baseline responses from women in North India.

Evaluating profile-conditioned sensitivity by measuring whether LLMs can accurately preserve behavioral variations and nuances across different demographic and household profiles (e.g., varying age, education, income, family structure, and religion) rather than just outputting population-level averages.
